existing.selection_notes: Six scholarships are available. Awards are made against the published eligibility conditions, which turn on three things: holding a firm offer for full-time study, UK location with Home or RUK fee status, and a qualifying asylum, refugee-protection, discretionary-leave or UK resettlement scheme status. The published page states that if you are unsure whether you are eligible to apply, you should contact the team using their enquiry form. No academic threshold, interview, assessment weighting or decision date is published.
existing.best_fit: People living in the UK with Home or RUK fee status who have claimed asylum in the UK, are appealing a refused asylum decision, hold refugee status, humanitarian protection or discretionary leave from an asylum claim, or arrived through a UK government resettlement scheme, and who hold a firm offer for full-time study at the University of Glasgow.
existing.notes: Accommodation is explicitly not included: the University states that University accommodation is not included in the Sanctuary Scholarship and that applicants will therefore need to cover their own accommodation costs or already live within a reasonable commuting distance of the University. The scholarship is not available to PGdip, PDGE or part time programmes. Award value varies by funding route: undergraduates with refugee status (or equivalent) and access to funding receive the £5,000 stipend towards study costs only; postgraduate taught masters students with refugee status (or equivalent) and access to funding receive the £5,000 stipend plus a partial tuition fee waiver to cover any shortfall not met by the Postgraduate Masters tuition fee loan. The University states that if your immigration status changes part way through your studies you should inform the Scholarships Team as soon as possible, as this may affect eligibility, that changes are reviewed on a case-by-case basis, and that the scholarship funding will not cease automatically but may be recalculated. The page contains an internal inconsistency: it states the offer requirement is for '2027/26' while the surrounding text describes the 2027/28 academic year, which appears to be a typographical error on the official page. The page also carries an eVisa notice referencing a BRP expiring on 31 December 2025, which is out of date relative to the current cycle.
existing.duration: Tuition fee waiver for the duration of the programme; £5,000 per year stipend
existing.application_period: For the 2027/28 academic year the scholarship is announced and not yet open for applications: the University states applications 'will open soon' and invites applicants to register their interest in the meantime. No opening date or closing date has been published for the 2027/28 cycle.
existing.deadline_display: Applications for this scholarship for the 2027-28 academic session will open soon. In the meantime please provide your details and we will be in touch when the scholarship is open for applications.
